features.description: Install `openclaw@2026.5.2` locally and harden it for personal laptop operation. Gateway binds to loopback by default, auth secrets stay outside git, Control UI is not exposed publicly, and `openclaw security audit --deep` becomes the baseline verification command.
steps: Install `openclaw@2026.5.2` with npm or the official installer.
Create or verify `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` with loopback bind and gateway auth.
Run `openclaw --version`, `openclaw doctor`, and `openclaw security audit --deep`.
Record any critical findings in this plan's INBOX before enabling external channels.
features.acceptance: (1) `openclaw --version` reports 2026.5.2. (2) Gateway binds to loopback or an explicitly documented tailnet-only endpoint. (3) Gateway auth token/password exists outside git. (4) `openclaw security audit --deep` is run and critical findings are resolved or documented.

features.description: Create OpenClaw workspace bootstrap files from the useful parts of Axiom's SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, and TOOLS.md. Keep identity, action tiers, dashboard reporting, group-chat boundaries, and security posture. Remove Cloudflare/R2/container/clawdbot-specific assumptions.
steps: Create `~/.openclaw/workspace/SOUL.md` from trimmed Axiom SOUL.md.
Create `~/.openclaw/workspace/AGENTS.md` with action tiers, memory boundaries, dashboard reporting, and group-chat behavior.
Create `~/.openclaw/workspace/TOOLS.md` with local OpenClaw, DontPanic, Axiom dashboard, GitHub, and messaging references.
Add a DontPanic operations section that lists allowed and approval-required commands.
Document canonical DontPanic paths (`~/.dontpanic`, `.dontpanic/dontpanic.json`) and legacy Jarvis fallback paths.
features.acceptance: (1) SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, and TOOLS.md exist in the OpenClaw workspace. (2) Cloudflare/R2/container/clawdbot-specific references are removed or rewritten. (3) Group-chat memory and owner-approval boundaries are explicit. (4) Canonical DontPanic paths/env vars are documented, with Jarvis paths/env vars marked legacy fallback.

features.description: Expose DontPanic to OpenClaw through a narrow command wrapper rather than arbitrary shell. The wrapper supports status, plan intake, dispatch preview, and owner-approved gate operations, while refusing destructive or free-form commands from shared channels.
steps: Design an allowlisted wrapper for `dontpanic ps`, quota/caps status, plan status, and dispatch dry-run. Keep the legacy `jarvis` alias as a compatibility fallback only.
Discover DontPanic through `~/.dontpanic/agent-manifest.json` when present.
Require owner approval for `dispatch --confirm`, `approve`, and `resume`.
Refuse arbitrary shell passthrough and log denied attempts.
Test wrapper behavior from local shell before exposing through Discord or Telegram.
features.acceptance: (1) DontPanic status commands can be invoked through a narrow wrapper. (2) Dispatch confirmation and gate approval are owner-only operations. (3) No arbitrary shell passthrough is exposed to Discord, Telegram, or WhatsApp. (4) The wrapper prefers canonical DontPanic module/paths and only reads legacy Jarvis paths as fallback.

features.description: Personal-axiom configuration of the team dashboard. The actual sync layer + Firebase repointing + Cloud Functions + drag-flip MCP wiring all live in plan 2026-05-09-004 (`feat-team-dashboard-sync`) — that's the adapter plan. THIS feature is the personal-axiom-specific configuration: confirm jarvis-a6ee1 is the right Firebase target, ensure the operator's local DontPanic project_id is registered, document which dashboard views the operator wants enabled (Mission Control kanban + Security Approval Queue likely; Financial Analysis archived since it was Axiom's other use case). No code in DontPanic; no code in axiom adapter. Just operator-side configuration choices that the adapter plan reads. Per the architectural critique on 2026-05-09 (D008), DontPanic core stays neutral; sync layer is the adapter's domain. Originally this feature included the full sync work; that scope is now in plan 2026-05-09-004.
steps: Confirm jarvis-a6ee1 Firebase project is the dashboard target (per memory: Storage + Firestore APIs already enabled).
Verify operator's DontPanic project_id is registered (`dontpanic projects list`).
Document which dashboard views are enabled for the personal-axiom stack — typically Mission Control kanban + Security Approval Queue; Financial Analysis archived.
Add references to plan 2026-05-09-003 (projection contract) and plan 2026-05-09-004 (adapter implementation) as the load-bearing dependencies.
Capture which seed Firestore docs are needed for the dashboard's initial render (an empty `projects/<id>/plans` is acceptable; sync daemon will populate).
features.acceptance: (1) Operator-side configuration recorded — Firebase target, project_id, enabled dashboard views, archived views. (2) Plan 2026-05-09-003 (state projection) and plan 2026-05-09-004 (team-dashboard-sync) are listed as dependencies. (3) Zero DontPanic core code change in this feature. (4) Zero adapter code change in this feature (that's plan 2026-05-09-004). (5) Per architectural critique D008, this feature confirms scope split happened and references downstream.

features.description: Configure Discord as the primary shared project workspace for friends who run their own local DontPanic instances. Deconfliction uses GitHub issues, branches, PRs, DontPanic plan ids, and Discord threads. Telegram remains owner-private; WhatsApp remains optional notification-only.
steps: Document Discord server/category/channel naming conventions.
Document the invariant: one task = one GitHub issue + one DontPanic plan + one branch + one Discord thread.
Configure OpenClaw Discord allowlists and group mention requirements.
Ensure shared Discord channels cannot approve owner-only or destructive operations.
features.acceptance: (1) Discord server/channel convention is documented. (2) One task = one GitHub issue + one DontPanic plan + one branch + one Discord thread is documented. (3) Shared Discord channels cannot approve owner-only or destructive actions.

features.description: OpenClaw notification router skill — `dontpanic-notification-router` — that subscribes to DontPanic NotifyEvents (channel-agnostic) and fans out to the operator's channels per policy. DontPanic emits a single outbound NotifyEvent surface (kind + severity + plan_id + body + action_link, per plan 2026-05-01-002 F002); OpenClaw absorbs ALL per-channel knowledge (Discord webhooks, Telegram bot API, WhatsApp business API). The router applies policy: info+plan-boundary events → shared coordination channel (Discord); action_required+escalation events → owner-private channel (Telegram); optional after-hours mirror → WhatsApp. Bidirectional: when an operator replies in any channel (e.g. `/dp status`, `/dp inbox <plan>`), the router maps it to a DontPanic MCP tool call (from plan 2026-05-03-003 F002). Owner-only state changes (approve / resume / dispatch confirm) are gated on channel-AND-identity: Discord can only fire read-only commands; only Telegram private DM (or Control UI) can fire owner-approval commands per D003+D004. This absorbs the bidirectional Discord scope deferred in plan 2026-05-01-002 AND replaces the need for DontPanic to ever ship Telegram/WhatsApp-specific sinks. DontPanic keeps its built-in direct Discord sink as a no-OpenClaw solo-dev convenience (per plan 2026-05-01-002, status:completed); for THIS personal-axiom stack, the operator drops the direct DontPanic→Discord config and points DontPanic's webhook at OpenClaw's local receiver instead (Path A) OR has OpenClaw watch `INBOX.md` for new events (Path B, pull-based). Path B is recommended for personal-axiom because it survives OpenClaw restarts cleanly and avoids local-port management.
steps: Choose subscription mode: Path A (DontPanic webhook → OpenClaw receiver) or Path B (OpenClaw watches INBOX.md). Path B recommended for personal-axiom — record the choice in this plan's decisions.jsonl.

Create OpenClaw skill `~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/dontpanic-notification-router/SKILL.md` with: (a) NotifyEvent ingestion (Path A: HTTP receiver; Path B: file watcher on `<plan>/INBOX.md`), (b) policy table mapping event severity+kind→channel set, (c) per-channel renderers (Discord embed shape, Telegram MarkdownV2, WhatsApp template).

Configure operator-side per-channel routing in `~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/dontpanic-notification-router/config.json` (gitignored): channel IDs, bot tokens (referenced by env name only), allowlists per channel.

Implement bidirectional command surface — operator messages in any channel → router parses intent → calls DontPanic MCP tool (`approve_gate` / `dispatch` / `status` / `read_evidence` / etc.). Read-only commands (`status`, `inbox`, `dispatch --dry-run`) allowed in shared channels (Discord); owner-only commands (`approve`, `resume`, `dispatch --confirm`) gated to Telegram private DM + identity allowlist per D003+D004.

Wire the skill's MCP client at `~/.openclaw/mcp.json` with `dontpanic mcp serve` as a tool source. The DontPanic agent-manifest from plan 2026-05-03-003 F001 is the discovery file the skill reads on first run.

If using Path A: drop the direct `~/.dontpanic/discord.json` from the personal-axiom stack and point DontPanic's webhook at `http://127.0.0.1:<openclaw-port>/notify`. If Path B: leave `~/.dontpanic/discord.json` unset entirely.

Document the policy table in `~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/dontpanic-notification-router/POLICY.md`: severity+kind matrix → channel set → renderer. Include the rationale that per-channel routing is policy, not delivery — it lives in OpenClaw because OpenClaw owns the chat-surface domain.
Test offline first: mock NotifyEvent ingestion + each channel renderer + each MCP-tool dispatch + reject-non-allowlisted-user. Only after offline tests pass, enable live channels.
features.acceptance: (1) Skill exists at `~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/dontpanic-notification-router/` with SKILL.md, config.json (operator-supplied, gitignored), POLICY.md, and SECURITY.md. (2) Skill ingests DontPanic NotifyEvents via Path A (local HTTP) OR Path B (INBOX.md watcher) — choice recorded in decisions.jsonl. (3) Policy table maps severity+kind to channel set (e.g. info+plan_boundary → Discord; action_required+escalation → Telegram; optional WhatsApp mirror) and is editable WITHOUT code changes. (4) Bidirectional commands: read-only (`status`, `inbox`, `dispatch --dry-run`) allowed in Discord; owner-only state changes (`approve`, `resume`, `dispatch --confirm`) gated to Telegram private DM + Discord-user-ID allowlist per D003+D004. (5) Skill calls DontPanic exclusively through the MCP surface from plan 2026-05-03-003 F002 — no shell passthrough, no direct file reads of plan dirs (except INBOX.md watching when in Path B mode). (6) Non-allowlisted users in any channel are silently ignored (no reply — avoids confirming the bot's presence). (7) DontPanic itself is unchanged — no new emit points, no new MCP tools, no per-channel sinks beyond the existing Discord webhook (which stays for the no-OpenClaw solo-dev case). The router replaces the need for Telegram/WhatsApp sinks inside DontPanic. (8) Offline test fixture covers each policy-row × each channel renderer + at least three rejection cases (unknown command / non-allowlisted user / malformed args).
